name: Custom Hardware Units
text:
# Custom Hardware Units

## Overview
Custom Hardware Units implement [direct volume ray casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) by offloading the entire rendering pipeline to dedicated application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) or field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), rather than relying on general-purpose CPUs or programmable GPUs [G]. This family addresses the historical computational bottleneck where software implementations consumed excessive time on geometry calculations and [compositing](#2436-compositing.md), enabling real-time frame rates for regular data sets through highly parallel, fixed-function logic [G]. Unlike general-purpose GPU implementations that use texture sampling and fragment shaders, these units employ custom address generation, precalculated weight memories, and dedicated Digital Signal Processors (DSPs) to handle [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md), shading, and compositing in hardware [G].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Hardware-based Geometry Unit Resampling](3139-hardware-based-geometry-unit-resampling.md)
Offloads perspective calculations, [gradient estimation](#6476-gradient-estimation-our-grad.md), and volume data resampling to dedicated hardware accelerators using custom address generation and precalculated weight memories. It solves the bottleneck where software implementations consume up to 80% of computation time on these tasks. Choose this when high-throughput gradient estimation and [backward mapping](#3009-backward-mapping-ray-tracing.md) interpolation are required without general-purpose shader overhead.

### [Hardware-based Direct Volume Ray Casting](5442-hardware-based-direct-volume-ray-casting.md)
Offloads ray casting, shading, and compositing to dedicated programmable DSPs, decoupling these operations from general-purpose processors. It uses specialized DSPs to compute light-material interactions with high throughput, distinct from tree-based hardware methods by using sequential scanline processing per DSP. Choose this for high-throughput light-material [interaction](#41-interaction.md) calculations in [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md) data.

### [Custom Hardware Rendering](5746-custom-hardware-rendering.md)
Implements the entire [volume rendering pipeline](#1318-volume-rendering-pipeline.md) via dedicated ASICs or FPGAs, addressing the need for real-time rendering when CPUs/GPUs lacked sufficient throughput. It achieves interactive frame rates through highly parallel, regular computation, often using multiple identical pipelines. Choose this for fixed-function, high-performance rendering of regular datasets where flexibility is secondary to speed.

## Background
Custom hardware units emerged in the 1990s and early 2000s to address the limitations of CPU-based volume rendering, which was too slow for interactive applications [G]. Architectures such as Cube, Vizard, and VolumePro utilized dedicated hardware to achieve real-time performance for regular grid data [G]. These systems were largely superseded by the rise of programmable GPUs, which offered greater flexibility and comparable performance for many tasks, though custom hardware remains relevant in specific high-throughput or low-latency applications [G].
